source.title: JPL Solar System Dynamics, Planetary Satellite Mean Elements
source.licenceNote: Mean elements, physical data and GM are NASA/JPL numbers published without a licence statement; they are facts cited with their source, as the other JPL-sourced data in this project is. The source page asks that its elements not be used for ephemeris computation.

plane.note: Laplace plane pole as JPL tabulates it.

parentBody.source: JPL Horizons physical data, https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api, raw docs/evidence/o019-t078-horizons-20261017T035154Z/neptune-phys.txt: GM (km^3/s^2) = 6835099.97 (Horizons physical data for Neptune 899)

bodyPhysical.source: JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters, https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/phys_par/, accessed 2026-10-17, raw docs/evidence/o019-t078-sats-phys-20261017T035359Z/sats-phys.html

rotation.model: IAU WGCCRE 2015 (Archinal et al. 2018, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 130:22), as transcribed in NAIF pck00011.tpc
rotation.epoch: J2000 (2000-01-01 12:00 TDB); T in Julian centuries, d in days

periodicTerms.note: Coefficient k multiplies sin or cos of the k-th nutation-precession angle (RA and W: sin; Dec: cos) of the parent system; angles are in nutationPrecessionAngles as [constant, perCentury] pairs. Not used by the offline test.

rotation.note: Triton rotates synchronously; the report gives its model with the Neptune system nutation-precession angles.

model.note: The body turns synchronously, so its sidereal mean motion is the IAU prime-meridian rate (rotation.primeMeridianDeg.perDay); the semi-major axis is the one whose two-body period equals it. The table's own P is the sidereal period for the Saturn rows but not for the Jovian rows (Europa: 3.525 d against 3.551 d), so it is not used.

accuracy.comparedWith: JPL Horizons vectors, planet-centred (body centre), ICRF treated as EQJ, geometric, UTC
accuracy.classRule: within one diameter: largest error at most the body's mean diameter; approximate demonstration: at most one tenth of the semi-major axis; otherwise not usable as published
knownLimitations: Retrograde (inclination 157.3 degrees to the Laplace plane) with a node that precesses once in 340 years: one fixed ellipse cannot follow it.

The tabulated angles are given to 0.1 degree and e is 0.000, so the phase is an argument of latitude; a 4 degree phase shift at the epoch (25 thousand km) explains most of the error there, and the rate error (table P 5.876994 d against the IAU rate period 5.876854 d) adds the drift to 33.6 thousand km by 2030. The cause of the 4 degree phase offset was not found.
Horizons uses nep098_merged; the table is derived from NEP097.
